gaps.fact: Saccharomyces cerevisiae is the species of yeast for wine fermentation. The fermentation-yeast technique article (how) and its card teach it, but neither bank asks it of wine: the Régionale bank offers it only as a sake distractor (i-gunnxjxs) and the Village Beer & Cider chapter names it for ales, while the vin chapter and the two Village chapters name strains, ambient yeast and the pied de cuve without the species.

Barrel sizes as the Court prints them, as one ladder: barrique 225 litres, puncheon 300, demi-muid 600, foudre or botti 1,000 and more, and which has more flavour impact. The Village chapter gives barrique 225 and pièce 228 and leaves the foudre unsized; c-6i2c510m gives the demi-muid at about six hundred litres and c-hln4baio the Mosel Fuder at about a thousand; the one puncheon stem (c-71ptmz2m) gives 500 litres against the Court's 300. Botti in Piemonte and barriques in Rioja are taught in the piedmont and rioja articles.

Other woods used for barrels (acacia, cherry and chestnut) and Slavonian oak among the origins of oak. No stem in either bank and no chapter fact carries them: the region drill stem r-yy6vfg7c (Maipo) names the three woods in its explanation and the piedmont, campania and tuscany articles name Slavonian botti. French forests (Tronçais, Limousin) and American oak are asked at both levels.
How sustainability is implemented in the winery: energy and water use, lighter glass, waste and by product handling, certification.

The grid link: which regions and grapes carry lees or autolysis (Champagne, Muscadet, white Burgundy), malolactic (most reds, oaked Chardonnay; not Riesling or Sauvignon Blanc) and carbonic maceration (Beaujolais) as non fruit descriptors, and which do not.
Water addition as a winemaking term (lowering must sugar in hot regions where the law allows it).
Containers (bottles, kegs, boxed wine), closures (cork, composites, Stelvin screwcap, Vinolok glass top) and capsule colours and design; the Codex teaches cork, screwcap and technical cork only.

errors.where: js/data-questions.js, question c-71ptmz2m (cat Viticulture & Winemaking): 'More than double a barrique in one cask, the 500-litre format lets Syrah producers buy oak's slow breathing without its vanilla shouting. Name the format.' answer 'Puncheon'
errors.correction: The Court's curriculum fixes the puncheon at 300 litres (page 7, Fermentation Vessels Types, the Barrel Sizes list), the figure the Certified paper marks. The 500 litre puncheon the stem describes is Australian and Rhône trade usage, so the stem should carry the Court's 300 litres or ask by description without a litre figure.
errors.source: Court curriculum guide page 7, Fermentation Vessels Types, Barrel Sizes (the Court's puncheon figure is 300); trade usage of the term varies between 300 and 500 litres

courtUpdates.now: Since 8 December 2023 the European Union requires an ingredients list and a nutrition declaration for wine (Regulation (EU) 2021/2117 amending Regulation (EU) 1308/2013): the energy value must appear on the label itself and the rest may be given by electronic means such as a QR code; wine produced before that date is exempt.
courtUpdates.source: Regulation (EU) 2021/2117; Wine Institute webinar on EU ingredient labelling, September 2023; Food Safety Magazine, December 2023

notes: Mapped questions: Régionale 119 (Viticulture & Winemaking 69, Winemaking Techniques 50), Village 61 (Viticulture & Winemaking 29, Wine Fundamentals 32), 180 in all; of these, 31 Régionale and 14 Village stems of Viticulture & Winemaking are cellar stems, the rest vineyard and shared with the viticulture subject. The Certified column is strongest on chemistry (Wine Fundamentals), extraction, lees, malolactic and sulphur, and thinnest on the Court's vessel row (sizes, other woods) and the species of yeast. Two Court cells to read with care in our own copy: the Court says saignée 'essentially doesn't exist anymore' where the Codex teaches it as a live rosé route (Régionale stems and the vin chapter); our e- questions should follow the Court's three methods (maceration time, blending for sparkling, saignée) without contradicting either. The Court's 'Bâttonage' is its own spelling. One search spent, on labelling law.
